manifest.name: dsh-cherry-bridge
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin bridging to Cherry Studio desktops over remote transport, with an experimental subagent that delegates the way DSH's own subagent does (Claude Code / Codex style) but runs the child on a Cherry Studio agent

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npm run build:client && npm pack --dry-run

bundle.text:
# dsh-cherry-bridge 插件（DSH Bundle patch）
#
# 作为 bundle 被合入 profile 时，自动插入本插件行。
# 插件把本机 DSH 桥接到局域网内的 Cherry Studio 桌面端：设备连接池、`cherry_*`
# 工具面，以及同源设置页 UI（`dsh.client`）。
#
# ⚠️ patch 的 `config` 是**整体替换**而非与 bundle 默认值合并：装配层必须对缺键
#    回落默认值（`src/index.ts` 的 `resolveBridgeConfig`，Task 10 落地）。因此这里
#    列出的键就是该 profile 下的**完整**配置面；删掉一个键不等于"沿用默认"，
#    而是让装配层用自己的默认值（二者当前一致，见下）。
#
# 键值与 spec §8 一致：
#   - perSessionCacheBytes：每个会话的本地订阅事件缓存上限（字节）。2 MiB。
#   - rateBudgetPerSecond：每设备二级平滑请求预算（请求/秒），与
#     `DeviceConnection` 默认值一致。桌面端共享额度在 ≤2.1.6 是 64 req/s，
#     ≥2.1.7 是 256 req/s；只有新版本把超限降级为单请求 RATE_LIMITED 拒绝，
#     旧版本直接以 close 1011 终止整条会话，故按更严格的一代取保守值。
#   - dataDir 故意不写：留空时装配层按 $DSH_HOME/cherry-remote 解析，
#     写死会让所有 profile 共用同一份设备档案。
#
# ⚠️ 行的 `id` / `name` 不是自由文本——宿主 `applyEntryPatches` 只追加顶层 insert 行，
#    再由 `declaredRows` / bundle-in-use 判定「本插件已装配」，两处都要求
#    `row.id == entry.options.id` **且** `row.name == entry.options.name`；缺 id 或
#    缺 name 的行会被**静默跳过**（不报错、不装配）。因此：
#      `id`   = 组合条目 id，必须严格等于 `src/index.ts` 导出的插件 `name`；
#      `name` = npm 包名（package.json `name`）。
#    这条不变式由 `tests/contract/contract.test.ts` 断言锁死。
- insert:
    - id: cherry-remote
      name: 'dsh-cherry-bridge'
      config:
        perSessionCacheBytes: 2097152
        rateBudgetPerSecond: 32

readme.text: [English](README.en.md) | **简体中文**

**把 DeepSeek Harness 桥接到 Cherry Studio 桌面端** — DSH 插件 在 DSH 会话里直接驱动局域网内 Cherry Studio 的 agent：配对、列设备/会话、读历史、 发消息并等待终态、应答审批与提问卡、取消执行；附一个同源设置页管理设备与工具启用范围。 另含一项**实验性、默认关闭**的能力：**参照 DSH 官方 `subagent` 的委派方式**（与 Claude Code / Codex 的子智能体同一路数——把任务交给子 agent 执行，结果以文本回到父侧）实现了同类机制， **执行端换成 Cherry Studio 桌面端上的 agent**。见[实验性子智能体](#实验性子智能体)。 ```mermaid flowchart TB T["DSH 会话
15 个 cherry_* 工具"] --> P W["设置页
设备 · 配对 · 启用范围"] --> P P["dsh-cherry-bridge
连接池 · 订阅缓存 · 作用域"]

- 包名：`dsh-cherry-bridge`，插件 id：`cherry-remote`
- 传输：默认 `ws://` + Noise XX（加密由 Noise 记录层提供）；桌面端位于 TLS 前置之后时拨 `wss://`，私有 CA 的信任由 `wsTls` 提供
- 工具面：15 个 `cherry_*` 工具（第 15 个 `cherry_subagent` 是**实验性、默认关闭**的跨端委派，见[实验性子智能体](#实验性子智能体)），**按工作区**启用，默认**谁都没有**（见「启用范围」）
- 设置页与 HTTP 面：宿主 Web 服务器上的同源前缀 `/cherry-remote/api`

> **DSH 版本需求**：`>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`（由 `package.json` 的 `engines.dsh` 声明；不满足时 bundle 被跳过、设置页里该插件的行被禁用，确需在区间外使用可用 `dsh plugin allow-version` 精确豁免。0.3.0 需重新评估兼容性后再放开）。
>
> **Cherry Studio 兼容范围**：桌面端 **2.1.4 – 2.1.10 已核对**——`v3` 自定义地址二维码需 **2.1.8+**，2.1.4–2.1.7 的 `v2` 二维码同样可用。2.1.9/2.1.10 与 2.1.8 在 remote-access 面上只差桌面端发送链的一处健壮性修复（PR #22593，不影响客户端），并在 2.1.10 真机上跑过「建会话 → 发送 → 等待 → 读取」冒烟。区间外未经验证：握手只协商协议版本 `[1]`，不兼容时会以 `unreachable` 明确失败，不会静默出错。协议包钉在 `0.7.0` / `0.2.5`，2.1.10 携带的还是同一对版本。

```bash

readme.section: 从 npm 安装（推荐，钉住版本）
readme.text: npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cherry-bridge@0.2.3

readme.section: 安装 npm 最新发布版
readme.text: npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cherry-bridge

readme.section: 从 GitHub 源码安装（与 npm 发布同一提交）

npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:SAXEM1997/dsh-cherry-bridge#v0.2.3
```

本包自带 `cordis.patch.yml`（`package.json` 的 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向它），
dsh-plugin-manager 据此自动插入插件行。手工加行等价于：
yaml
- id: cherry-remote
  name: 'dsh-cherry-bridge'
  config:
    perSessionCacheBytes: 2097152
    rateBudgetPerSecond: 32
```

1. 在 Cherry Studio 桌面端打开 **remote access → 添加设备**：该界面显示**二维码**，
   配对信息要点开扫码后的页面才看得到。
2. **扫这个二维码**（微信、浏览器等均可），复制页面上显示的配对信息。
3. 在 DSH 里调用 `cherry_pair`（设置页向导亦可），粘贴这段配对信息。
4. **双向核对 6 位验证码**：与桌面端显示的数字人工比对一致后再在桌面端批准。
5. 批准后设备档案写入数据目录（`devices.json`，`0600`），其 `desktopIdentity` 被 pin 住，
   此后每次连接都校验 Noise 对端静态公钥与 pin 一致，防二维码被劫持后的中间人替换。

```text
cherry_pair → 粘贴扫码页的配对信息，核对 6 位验证码
cherry_devices → 看设备与连接状态（前缀即可选中，如 "dev-A"）
cherry_agents → 列设备上的 agent，拿 agentId
cherry_sessions → 列某 agent 的会话，拿 sessionId

| 键 | 类型 | 默认 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataDir` | string | `$DSH_HOME/cherry-remote`（回退 `~/.dsh/cherry-remote`） | 插件数据目录，存放 `identity.key` 与 `devices.json`（均 `0600`）。 |
| `perSessionCacheBytes` | number | `2097152`（2 MiB） | 每个会话的**本地**订阅事件缓存上限；超出后从最旧一端丢弃（FIFO）并 `warn`，但**最新的单条事件总会保留**——即使它自己就超过上限（此时不打丢弃日志，窗口保持超预算）。 |
| `rateBudgetPerSecond` | number | `32` | 每设备平滑请求预算（请求/秒）。桌面端共享额度在 ≤2.1.6 是 64 req/s、≥2.1.7 是 256 req/s，且只有新版本才把超限降级为单请求 `RATE_LIMITED`（旧版本直接 close `1011` 终止会话），故按更严格的一代取保守值。内容读取（`agent.content.read`）按 8:1 派生独立一档，且**封顶 512/s**（该额度两代一致）。 |
| `wsTls` | object | — | 每次 `wss` 拨号的**扁平** `tls.connect` 选项（只接受 `rejectUnauthorized` / `ca`），供桌面端位于私有 CA 或自签 TLS 前置之后时由运维提供信任；配对与重连**两个拨号点**共用。**不写入设备档案、不写日志、不进诊断报告。** 整个对象要么按原样生效、要么整体忽略：未知键或不可用值按名 `warn` 后回退 Node 默认信任库（不部分应用）。 |
| `subagent` | object | — | 实验性子智能体的 profile 种子（**默认关闭**）。字段与行为见[实验性子智能体](#实验性子智能体)；设置页保存过配置后，`<dataDir>/subagent.json` 优先于本键。 |

> `wsTls.ca` 是 **PEM 内容**（证书文本本身），不是文件路径。

> ⚠️ `cordis.patch.yml` 的 `config` 是**整体替换**，不与默认值合并。删掉一个键得到的是
> 插件默认值；键存在但值非法（`0`、负数、字符串）会按名 `warn` 后回落默认值。

| 工具 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `cherry_devices` | 列出已配对设备及连接状态（`connected`/`connecting`/`offline`/`disabled`/`identity-mismatch`）。`action: "forget"` 可遗忘指定地址（从拨号列表移除，且桌面再广播也不会被重新学习，直到 `remember` 或重新配对）；`action: "remember"` 撤销该标记（下次握手可重新学习）；两者都需要 `device` 与 `hosts`。 |
| `cherry_agents` | 列出某设备上可用的 agent（分页）。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`（`limit` 或 `safety-bound`，后者是 1000 条内部上限）；停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用同一 device 与过滤条件把它回传为 `cursor` 即可从停点继续（此时 `limit` 约束的是下一次回答）；跨工具/设备/过滤条件的令牌会被**本地拒绝**，不会转发给对端。 |
| `cherry_workspaces` | 列出某 agent 的**已注册**工作区，以及是否存在系统工作区。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`；停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用相同过滤条件回传为 `cursor` 即可续读。 |
| `cherry_sessions` | 列出某 agent 的会话，可按工作区过滤。被截断时必带 `truncated`+`truncationReason`（`limit` 或 `safety-bound`），停点可命名时还给出 `resumeCursor`——用同一 device 与**相同过滤条件**把它回传为 `cursor` 即可从停点继续（此时 `limit` 约束的是下一次回答）；跨工具/设备/过滤条件的令牌会被**本地拒绝**。 |
| `cherry_read` | 读会话消息历史快照，**从新到旧**返回（`limit` 丢掉的是**最旧**的消息）。失败消息在桌面端给出时附带 `failure: {reasonCode, retryable, message}`（对端分类、是否值得重试、对端自己的有界摘要；其 `source`/`context` 不投影到回答里）。附件 part 只回 `name`/`mediaType`/`byteLength`，`content` 为空——字节不取。这覆盖桌面端可能发来的两种形状：`file` part（`name` 即文件名，`byteLength` 取自它的 ref）；以及桌面端用于**未上传**附件的旧

`device` 参数接受**精确 `deviceId`**，或 **`deviceId` 前缀 / 显示名前缀**；多项命中返回
`ambiguous-device` + `candidates`，一个都没命中返回 `not-found` + `known`。

`cherry_send(wait: true)` / `cherry_wait` 的 `status` 有 **8 个取值**：四个协议终态
（`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`/`interrupted`），加上 `awaiting-interaction`（出现待答
交互卡，运行仍活着）、`timeout`（窗口用尽，**不是失败**，随附部分内容，停点可命名时再带游标）、
`idle`（`cherry_wait` 遇到没有在途执行的会话，立即返回快照）、`subscription-lost`
（事件订阅丢失且重建失败，运行结局**不可知**，随附修复指引）。

终态回答在对端给出失败分类时附带 `executionError: {reason, message?}`——**只保留这两个字段**，
`details` / `failure` 这类协议留空的部分不会进入模型上下文。

> 实验性功能：仿 DSH 官方 subagent 的委派方式（与 Claude Code / Codex 的子智能体同一路数），把任务交给 Cherry Studio 桌面端上的 agent 执行、结果以文本回来。它跨了 DSH 与 Cherry Studio 两个不受本插件控制的系统，接口与行为都可能变。默认关闭。
>
> 欢迎贡献思路和问题反馈：[dsh-cherry-bridge issues](https://github.com/SAXEM1997/dsh-cherry-bridge/issues)

打开方式：设置页的「实验性子智能体」区块，或 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的 `subagent` 键：

```yaml
subagent:
  enabled: true
  device: desk-1        # deviceId，或足以指向一台设备的前缀（与其余工具同形）
  agentId: agent-7      # 该设备上的 Cherry agent id

**保存或改配置后要重启 DSH 才生效**：工具在装配期注册，本插件不热重载。页面上的保存写进
`<dataDir>/subagent.json`（`0600`、原子写入、`revision` 单调），一旦存在就优先于 profile 里的
`subagent` 键。

打开后模型多一个 `cherry_subagent` 工具：把一个自包含任务交给那台设备上的 Cherry agent，工具
**立即返回**，子运行结束时由运行时通知。子会话**看不到当前对话**，也**不接受后续消息**——它需要
的一切都得写进 `prompt`。

设置页编辑 `enabled` / `device` / `agentId` / 工作区 / `timeoutMs`（默认 30 分钟，`0` 表示不限）；
`providerName`、`toolName`、`cwdMode`、`routes`、`maxInteractionAbandons` 只透传——`routes` 只读展示
（它按子目录前缀覆盖设备与工作区），其余几个要改就走配置文件。

已知限制：

- **一次性**：没有后续消息、没有冷恢复、没有结构化输出、没有进度流；中途进度只能事后 `cherry_read`。
- **无沙箱继承**：子运行在 Cherry Studio 自己的权限模型下，DSH 的 sandbox 与审批 UI 都不适用。
- **子可能拒绝任务**：Cherry agent 有自己的角色边界。拒绝是一次**正常完成的运行**，返回的文本就是
  拒绝本身——不是故障；重试或改写任务前先读回答。
- **容量未知**：只实测了 3 路并行；更高并发下 Cherry 侧是否限流未验证。

它和其余 `cherry_*` 工具一样受「启用范围」约束：被排除的工作区看不到它。

- 读方法在重连后**单次**重放；桌面端 ≥2.1.7 的限流拒绝（`RATE_LIMITED` + `retryAfterMs`）
  也在调用方预算内等待后**单次**重放。**命令永不重放**——写操作丢失应答时，携**原 `commandId`**
  重试即可，桌面端的命令账本会回放原回执。命令被限流拒绝是另一回事：桌面端在**派发前**就拒绝，
  命令根本没执行，错误文本会说明这一点、给出对端要求的等待时间（`retryAfterMs`，对端没给就不写），
  并提示该检查的 `rateBudgetPerSecond`（默认预算远到不了限流）。
- 单个外置内容上限 32 MiB，超过的 part 标 `unavailable`，不回无法校验的部分内容。
- **外置内容装配是进程级限流的**：同时最多 4 个 `{ref}` 在装配（官方客户端的读并发策略）。
  单个 ref 的装配峰值约 3× 它的大小，所以**装配峰值**上界是 4×3×32 MiB = 384 MiB，日常远低于此
  （4×3×声明大小）。它约束的是**正在装配**的内容，不是全部驻留：已经装配完、被各调用自己持有的内容
  不在这个乘积里（每次并发读最多再带一整条消息，因为输出预算只在消息之间检查），parts 缓存另计。
  等待槽位也计入等待类回答的时限：排到时限就放弃并把这一 part 标 `unavailable`。
- 历史走查被截断时一定说明（`truncationReason`，`limit` / `aggregate-bytes` / `deadline` 三种含义不同，见上），
  并在停点可命名时给出 `messagesResumeCursor` 续读令牌。**停点不可命名时就不给**：对端位置为空、
  带首尾空白或任意控制字符、形如已停用的 v1 令牌、令牌会超过 4096 字符上限、或没有可当锚点的
  消息 id——此时 `truncated` 仍为 `true`，**缺失本身不代表历史已到底**。补救按 `truncationReason`
  分：`limit` 停点只有在调用方自己握着上限时才靠更宽的 `limit`（`cherry_read` 与四个列表工具）；
  **wait 类回答的 `limit` 是它自己的固定条数额度**，更旧的历史要用 `cherry_read` 去读。
  `aggregate-bytes` 停点不行——预算是它停下的原因，更宽的 `limit` 只会多付往返，被挡住的旧消息
  在这一回答里拿不到；`safety-bound` 停点是内部熔断，调用方动不了它；`deadline`（只出现在 wait
  类回答）同样改用 `cherry_read` 续读，它没有时限。
  **两个面是同一条规
> 传输重放、32 MiB/≈3× 内存、空页与游标容忍、完整性语义等工程细节见 [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md)。

插件同时是 **web client bundle**（`package.json` 的 `dsh.client`，导出 `./client`），通过
`settings.section` 槽位注册 **`cherry-remote`**（导航标签「Cherry 互联」）页面：
设备卡片（启用/停用/删除，地址的「忘记 / 恢复」）、配对向导（粘贴 → 6 位验证码 → 终态）、
启用范围面板，以及经
`/cherry-remote/api/events` SSE 推送的实时状态。

15 个工具**按工作区**决定是否出现，机制是**隐藏而非拒绝**（不在范围的会话里不进工具表，省上下文）。
第 15 个 `cherry_subagent` 的存在条件更严：实验开关打开、配置可用、宿主提供了子智能体服务，
**且该服务能承载这个工具**——缺 `startActivation`，或在装了启用范围门时缺 `tools.resolve`，
都按 fail-closed 不注册，状态里会写明是哪一个（`ready-without-tool` 的 `problem`）。

- **默认谁都没有**：作用域文档不存在、损坏或读不出来，都按 `selected` + 空列表处理（fail-closed）。
- **`仅选定工作区`**：只有勾选的工作区里的会话才可能出现这些工具；没有工作区的会话始终没有。
- **`全局`**：所有工作区都可见，面板勾选不参与判定。
- **保存即时生效**：对所有 live agent 重装/释放限制层，**下一轮**即生效，无需重启或新建会话。
- **范围只管工具**：设置页与 `/cherry-remote/api` 不受范围影响，被排除的工作区也能自救。
- **不假装**：宿主能力 `pending` / `unsupported` 时面板如实说明，这 14 个工具都**不注册**（fail-closed）。
  第 15 个 `cherry_subagent` 是唯一例外——它由子智能体子系统按自己的开关注册，所以不会因为 scope
  降级而消失；但它带一个**每步判定**的可见性条件，因此也不会因为降级就变成对所有工作区可见。

**Bridge DeepSeek Harness to Cherry Studio desktops** — a DSH plugin

Drive Cherry Studio agents on your LAN straight from a DSH session: pair, list
devices/sessions, read history, send messages and wait for a terminal state,
answer approval and question cards, cancel executions — plus a same-origin
settings page for device and tool-scope management.

It also carries one **experimental, off-by-default** capability: **it follows the
delegation shape of DSH's own `subagent`** — the same pattern as Claude Code /
Codex subagents, where a task goes to a child agent and the result comes back as
text — with **the child running on a Cherry Studio desktop agent** instead. See
[Experimental subagent](#experimental-subagent).

```mermaid flowchart TB T["DSH sessions
15 cherry_* tools"] --> P W["Settings page
devices · pairing · scope"] --> P P["dsh-cherry-bridge
pool · subscriptions · scope"]

- Package: `dsh-cherry-bridge`, plugin id: `cherry-remote`
- Transport: `ws://` + Noise XX by default (encryption lives in the Noise record layer); a desktop behind a TLS front is reached over `wss://`, with `wsTls` supplying the private-CA trust
- Tool face: 15 `cherry_*` tools — the fifteenth, `cherry_subagent`, is the **experimental, off-by-default** cross-desktop delegation (see [Experimental subagent](#experimental-subagent)) — enabled **per workspace**, and by default **nobody has them** (see “Scope”)
- Settings page and HTTP face: the same-origin prefix `/cherry-remote/api` on the host web server

> **DSH version requirement**: `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` (declared via `engines.dsh` in `package.json`; when unmet the bundle is skipped and its settings-page row disabled — `dsh plugin allow-version` grants an explicit exemption; 0.3.0 needs a fresh compatibility pass before the range widens).
>
> **Cherry Studio compatibility**: desktop **2.1.4 – 2.1.10 is verified** — the `v3` custom-address QR needs **2.1.8+**, and the `v2` QR of 2.1.4 – 2.1.7 works too. 2.1.9/2.1.10 differ from 2.1.8 on the remote-access face by exactly one robustness fix in the desktop's write chain (PR #22593, no client impact), and were smoke-tested on a real 2.1.10 (create a session → send → wait → read). Outside that range is unverified: the handshake negotiates protocol version `[1]` only, so an incompatible peer fails loudly as `unreachable` instead of misbehaving. The protocol packages are pinned to `0.7.0` / `0.2.5` — 2.1.10 still ships that same pair.

npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cherry-bridge@0.2.3
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-cherry-bridge

The package ships `cordis.patch.yml` (`package.json`'s `dsh.bundle.patch` points
at it); dsh-plugin-manager inserts the plugin line from it. The manual profile
line is equivalent to:yaml
- id: cherry-remote
  name: 'dsh-cherry-bridge'
  config:
    perSessionCacheBytes: 2097152
    rateBudgetPerSecond: 32
```

1. On the Cherry Studio desktop open **remote access → add device**: that
   screen shows a **QR code**; the pairing information only appears on the page
   the code leads to.
2. **Scan the QR code** (WeChat, any browser, …) and copy the pairing
   information the scanned page displays.
3. In DSH call `cherry_pair` (the settings-page wizard works too) and paste it.
4. **Cross-check the 6-digit verification code both ways** against the
   desktop's number before approving on the desktop side.
5. After approval the device archive is written to the data directory
   (`devices.json`, `0600`) with the `desktopIdentity` **pinned**; every later
   connection verifies the Noise peer static key against the pin, so a hijacked
   QR code cannot be traded for a man-in-the-middle substitute.

```text
cherry_pair → paste the pairing info from the scanned page, check the 6-digit code
cherry_devices → see devices and connection state (a prefix selects one, e.g. "dev-A")
cherry_agents → list the device's agents, take an agentId
cherry_sessions → list an agent's sessions, take a sessionId

| Key | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dataDir` | string | `$DSH_HOME/cherry-remote` (fallback `~/.dsh/cherry-remote`) | Plugin data directory holding `identity.key` and `devices.json` (both `0600`). |
| `perSessionCacheBytes` | number | `2097152` (2 MiB) | Per-session cap on the **local** subscription event cache; beyond it events are dropped from the oldest end (FIFO) with a `warn`, but the **newest single event is always kept** — even when it alone exceeds the cap (no drop line is logged then, and the window stays over budget). |
| `rateBudgetPerSecond` | number | `32` | Per-device smoothed request budget (req/s). The desktop's shared allowance is 64 req/s through 2.1.6 and 256 req/s from 2.1.7, and only the newer generation downgrades an overrun to a single `RATE_LIMITED` refusal (the older one terminates the session with close `1011`) — hence a value sized for the harsher generation. Content reads (`agent.content.read`) derive their own tier at 8:1, **capped at 512/s** (that allowance is the same in both generations). |
| `wsTls` | object | — | **Flat** `tls.connect` options for every `wss` dial (`rejectUnauthorized` / `ca` only): operator-supplied trust

> `wsTls.ca` is **PEM CONTENT** (the certificate text itself), not a file path.

> ⚠️ `cordis.patch.yml`'s `config` is **whole-replace**, not merged with the
> defaults. Removing a key gets you the plugin default; a key that exists but is
> unusable (`0`, negative, a string) falls back with a named `warn`.

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `cherry_devices` | List every paired device and its connection state (`connected`/`connecting`/`offline`/`disabled`/`identity-mismatch`). `action: "forget"` makes named addresses go away (removed from the dial list, and not re-learned when the desktop advertises them again, until `remember` or a re-pair); `action: "remember"` lifts that mark so the next handshake may learn them again. Both write actions require `device` and `hosts`. |
| `cherry_agents` | List the agents available on a device (paginated). A truncated answer always carries `truncated` + `truncationReason` (`limit` or `safety-bound`, the latter the 1000-item internal ceiling); when the stop point can be named it also carries a `resumeCursor`: replay it as `cursor` with the same device and filters to continue from that stop point (`limit` then bounds the next answer). A token from another tool, device or filter set is refused **locally**, never forwarded. |
| `cherry_workspaces` | List an agent's **registered** workspaces, and whether a system workspace exists. A truncated answer always carries `truncated` + `truncationReason`; when the stop point can be named it also carries a `

The `device` argument accepts an **exact `deviceId`**, or a **prefix of a
`deviceId` or of a display name**; several matches return `ambiguous-device` +
`candidates`, and no match returns `not-found` + `known`.

`cherry_send(wait: true)` / `cherry_wait` results carry one of **8 `status`
values**: the four protocol terminal states
(`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`/`interrupted`), plus `awaiting-interaction`
(a pending card appeared while the run is still alive), `timeout` (the window
ran out, **not a failure** — partial content comes back, plus a stop-point
cursor when one can be named), `idle` (`cherry_wait` met a session with nothing
in flight and returned the snapshot immediately), and `subscription-lost` (the
subscription was lost and could not be rebuilt, so the outcome is
**unknowable**; repair guidance ships with it).

A terminal answer carries `executionError: {reason, message?}` when the peer
supplied a failure classification — **only those two fields**: opaque parts the
protocol leaves unconstrained (`details`, `failure`) never reach a model's
context.

> Experimental: it delegates the way DSH's own subagent does — the same pattern as Claude Code / Codex subagents, where a task goes to a child agent and the result comes back as text — except the child runs on a Cherry Studio desktop agent. It spans two systems the plugin does not control, DSH and Cherry Studio, so its interface and behaviour may change. Off by default.
>
> Ideas and bug reports are welcome: [dsh-cherry-bridge issues](https://github.com/SAXEM1997/dsh-cherry-bridge/issues)

Turning it on: the settings page’s “Experimental subagent” block, or the
`subagent` key in `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
subagent:
  enabled: true
  device: desk-1        # a deviceId, or a prefix that names exactly one device
  agentId: agent-7      # a Cherry agent id on that device

**A save or a config edit takes effect when DSH restarts**: the tool is
registered during assembly, and this plugin does not hot-reload. A save on the
page writes `<dataDir>/subagent.json` (`0600`, atomic, monotonic `revision`),
which takes precedence over the profile’s `subagent` key as soon as it exists.

With it on, the model gains one `cherry_subagent` tool: it hands a self-contained
task to a Cherry agent on that desktop and **returns at once**; the runtime
notifies the parent when the child’s run ends. The child **does not see this
conversation** and **accepts no follow-up messages** — everything it needs has to
be in `prompt`.

The settings page edits `enabled` / `device` / `agentId` / workspace /
`timeoutMs` (30 minutes by default, `0` means no bound). `providerName`,
`toolName`, `cwdMode`, `routes` and `maxInteractionAbandons` are only carried
through — `routes` is shown read-only (it overrides the device and workspace per
directory prefix), the rest need the config file.

Known limits:

- **One-shot**: no follow-up messages, no cold recovery, no structured output, no
  progress stream; progress is `cherry_read` after the fact.
- **No sandbox inheritance**: the child runs under Cherry Studio’s own permission
  model; DSH’s sandbox and approval UI do not apply.
- **The child may decline the task**: Cherry agents have their own role
  boundaries. A refusal is a **normally completed run** whose text is the refusal
  — not a failure; read the answer before retrying or rewording.
- **Capacity is unverified**: only 3 concurrent delegations were exercised; a
  lower ceiling on the Cherry side at higher concurrency is not ruled out.

Like the other `cherry_*` tools it obeys the enabled scope: an excluded workspace
does not see it.

- Read methods are replayed **once** after a reconnect, and **once** after a
  desktop >= 2.1.7 rate-limit refusal (`RATE_LIMITED` + `retryAfterMs`, waited
  out within the caller's budget); **commands are never replayed** — a write
  that loses its reply is recovered by retrying with the **original
  `commandId`**, and the desktop's command ledger replays the receipt. A
  rate-limited COMMAND is the other case: the desktop refuses it **before
  dispatch**, so this attempt was never applied — the error text says so, names
  the wait the peer asked for (`retryAfterMs`, omitted when it sent none), and
  points at `rateBudgetPerSecond` (the default budget is far below the limit).
- One externalized content is capped at 32 MiB; a larger part is marked
  `unavailable` rather than returning unverifiable partial content.
- **Externalized-content assembly is gated process-wide**: at most 4 `{ref}`
  contents are assembled at once (the official client's read-concurrency
  policy). One ref's assembly peaks at ~3× its size, so the **assembly** peak is
  at most 4 × 3 × 32 MiB = 384 MiB worst case, and in ordinary traffic
  4 × 3 × (declared size). It bounds what is being ASSEMBLED, not everyt

> Engineering detail — replay rules, the 32 MiB/≈3× memory contract, empty-page
> and cursor tolerance, integrity semantics — lives in [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md).

The plugin is also a **web client bundle** (`package.json`'s `dsh.client`,
exporting `./client`). Through the `settings.section` slot it registers a
**`cherry-remote`** page (nav label “Cherry Bridge”): device cards
(enable/disable/remove, plus forget/restore for an address), a pairing wizard
(paste → 6-digit code → verdict), a scope panel, and live state pushed over the
same-origin SSE feed (`/cherry-remote/api/events`).

The 15 tools appear **per workspace**, by **hiding, not refusing** (in an
out-of-scope session they never enter the tool table, saving context). The
fifteenth, `cherry_subagent`, has stricter terms for existing at all: the
experiment on, its configuration usable, the host providing a subagent service,
**and that service able to honour the tool** — no `startActivation`, or no
`tools.resolve` while the scope gate is installed, and it is not registered
(fail-closed), with the status naming which one (`ready-without-tool`'s
`problem`):

- **Default is nobody**: a missing, corrupt or unreadable scope document is
  treated as `selected` + an empty list (fail-closed).
- **`Selected workspaces only`**: only sessions inside ticked workspaces can see
  the tools; sessions with no workspace never do.
- **`Global`**: visible everywhere; the ticks play no part.
- **Saves take effect immediately**: the restriction layer is re-installed or
  released for every live agent, effective from the **next turn** — no restart,
  no new session.
- **Scope governs tools only**: the settings page and `/cherry-remote/api` are
  never scope-gated, so an excluded workspace can rescue itself.
- **No pretending**: on `pending` / `unsupported` host capability the panel says
  so and the fourteen stay **unregistered** (fail-closed). The fifteenth,
  `cherry_subagent`, is the one exception — it is registered by the subagent
  subsystem on its own switch, so a scope degradation does not remove it; it
  carries a **per-step** visibility condition instead, so the degradation does
  not make it visible everywhere either.
